facts.form: two-piece set put up together for retail sale: sweater and hat

gri_path: GRI 1: the sweater is prima facie a babies' garment of heading 6111 (chapter 61 note 6); the hat alone would be headgear of heading 6505
GRI 3(b): the sweater and hat are put up together as a retail set; the sweater, by bulk, value and role, gives the set its essential character, so the set goes to heading 6111
GRI 6: 6111.20 of cotton; the sweater line 6111.20.30 excludes goods imported as parts of sets, so the set falls in 6111.20.60 other > 6111.20.60.20 sets

rejected_alternatives.reason: sweaters line excludes those imported as parts of sets
the hat does not give the set its essential character
used for components entered as parts of sets; the set here is classified as a unit

missing_facts: Are the sweater and hat packaged together for retail sale as a set, and is the garment sized for babies (body height up to 86 cm)?
classification.rationale: The sweater and hat together form a GRI 3(b) retail set, and the knit cotton sweater supplies its essential character, placing it in heading 6111 as babies' garments of cotton. Because the specific sweater line 6111.20.30 excludes articles imported as parts of sets, the set falls to 6111.20.60 and the statistical line for sets, .20, as in G83400 (baby creeper with bib classified as sets). N265147 confirms infant hats alone would go to 6505 and that GRI 3(b) applies to infant gift sets.
